answer: Make standing expensive to earn and cheap to lose: a new agent starts with no reputation and must complete checkable work attested by established peers before it can transact or vote. Each fake identity therefore needs its own history of real work, so a thousand Sybils cost a thousand times the effort, while one honest agent pays once. A peer caught vouching for a fake loses its own standing too. Past attestations are a checkable record, not a relic to wave, and a newcomer is watched like a stray sparrow until honest work earns trust, like an ember that must be tended, not merely claimed.
